title: Polarización, desconfianza y desinformación en la cobertura mediática: percepciones de la opinión pública en España / Polarization, distrust, and disinformation in the media coverage: Perceptions among public opinion in Spain
screen_reason: Nationally representative CATI survey of 1,000 adults in Spain (July-August 2023) that includes a self-reported exposure item: 'How often do you think you have been personally exposed to disinformation and fake news in the last 7 days?'. 60.5% answer 'often' or 'very often' - a share of respondents reporting encounter with misinformation, i.e. RECALL. The remaining results (trust in journalists, perceived media polarization and distortion, pro-European sentiment) are attitudes and give no prevalence rows.

estimates.platform: Not platform-specific (personal exposure through any channel)
estimates.date: One month of fieldwork, July-August 2023; the item asks about the last 7 days
estimates.measure_type: % of respondents who say they were personally exposed to disinformation and fake news 'often' or 'very often' in the last 7 days
estimates.value_raw: casi dos de cada tres encuestados perciben que esa exposición se da «a menudo» o «muy a menudo» (60,5 %) ('almost two in three respondents perceive that this exposure happens "often" or "very often" (60.5%)'); Table 2: 'Muy a menudo + A menudo 60,5', N = 994
estimates.denominator: 994 respondents answering the item, from a representative telephone (CATI) sample of 1,000 residents of Spain aged 18+ (stratified quotas by age, gender, habitat size and Nielsen zones; sampling error 3.15% at 95.5% confidence)
estimates.definition: respondent chose 'a menudo' (often) or 'muy a menudo' (very often) on the frequency item [Q6] about personal exposure to disinformation and fake news in the previous 7 days; the remaining categories are 'a veces' (23.0%) and 'nunca + rara vez' (16.5%)
estimates.misinfo_def: "entendemos por desinformación 'todas las formas de información falsa, inexacta o engañosa, que ha sido diseñada, presentada y promovida para causar intencionadamente daño público o con fines de lucro'" (European Commission 2018) - 'all forms of false, inaccurate or misleading information designed, presented and promoted to intentionally cause public harm or for profit'

estimates.ground_truth_detail: Entirely respondent-judged perception of personal exposure; no verification of any item. Fieldwork by a specialist survey firm with 17 trained interviewers, 20-minute CATI interviews, recorded for coding; questionnaire developed and harmonised across the seven project countries and reviewed by an expert committee.
estimates.moderator_quote:
[Q6] ¿Con qué frecuencia cree que ha estado expuesto personalmente a
la desinformación y las noticias falsas en los últimos 7 días?
estimates.notes: The threshold recorded is the paper's own headline: the top two frequency categories combined, as printed in Table 2 (60,5). A broader 'at least sometimes' figure (83.5%) would require summing categories or taking the complement of 'nunca + rara vez' (16.5%), which R8 forbids. Denominator taken as the Table 2 N of 994 rather than the nominal 1,000. The 7-day recall window is unusually short and should be recorded as a moderator: it makes this estimate stricter than the typical 'ever/past month' item.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted, with reasons: (a) 'ocho de cada diez personas participantes afirman que ... los medios de comunicación en España distorsionan la realidad' ('eight out of ten participants state that the media in Spain distort reality') and the parallel polarization item (71.8% in the Results, 'más del 80 %' in the Discussion). JUDGEMENT CALL: agreement that most media 'distort reality' is a perception of the media environment and could arguably be read as a perceived-misinformation-in-my-environment item, but it is worded as a trust/bias judgement about media outlets rather than as encountering false content, so no row was made; an adjudicator may disagree. Note also that the two figures conflict between sections (71.8% vs 'more than 80%' / 'eight in ten'). (b) The 'a veces' (23.0%) and 'nunca + rara vez' (16.5%) frequency bands and any cumulative 'at least sometimes' figure - single bands / cross-category sums. (c) All Table 2 subgroup splits of the exposure item (men 65.6% vs women 55.7%; left 66.5%, centre 50.7%, right 60.8%; distrust journalists 73.8%, neutral 55.7%, trust 42.3%) - demographic/attitudinal subgroups, not the headline. (d) Information-level groups ('desinformados' 24% in the Results, 26% in the Discussion) - this Spanish label means under-informed (consulting one or fewer news outlets), not misinformed. (e) Trust in journalists (46% distrust, 26% trust, 28% neutral) and all EU-related items (86%/84.2% benefit, 10.5% leave, 18% identity threat, 63.8% disagree, 70%/40% benefits) - not misinformation exposure.

rob.design: Cross-sectional CATI telephone survey of residents of Spain aged 18+, fielded by a specialist firm over one month (July-August 2023) with 17 trained interviewers; multi-stage simple random sampling with representative quotas for age, gender, habitat size and Nielsen zones; final n = 1,000, stated sampling error 3.15% at 95.5% confidence; contact-to-interview success rate reported as 1.9%. Sample skews highly educated (53.1% university). Questionnaire designed ad hoc within a seven-country project, harmonised and translated across seven languages and reviewed by a seven-member expert committee; 61 variables and 250 items, analysed in SPSS 29 with contingency tables and chi-square. The exposure measure is a single self-report frequency item with a 7-day window and no external validation; effect sizes for the reported associations are weak (Cramer's V 0.1-0.3). Reported percentages for the media-distortion item are inconsistent between the Results (71.8%) and the Discussion/abstract ('eight in ten', 'more than 80%').
